cleared.check: Slot0 packing: field offsets, mask widths, sign handling of the tick and the effect of dirty upper bits passed to a setter.
cleared.result: The four fields sit at bit offsets 0, 160, 184 and 208 with widths 160, 24, 24 and 24, so they end at bit 232 and do not overlap (src/types/Slot0.sol:33-38). MASK_160_BITS is written with 42 hex digits, two of them leading zeros, and equals 2^160 - 1. Every setter ANDs the new value with its mask before the shift and clears only its own field in the packed word (Slot0.sol:66-93). The tick getter sign extends from 24 bits (Slot0.sol:47-51). I transcribed the eight functions into Python and ran 200,000 random cases in which each setter received a full 256 bit value. Every getter returned the input truncated to the field width, the top 24 bits of the word stayed unchanged, and the order of the setters did not change the result. No caller-supplied value can spill into a neighbouring field. The repository test test/types/Slot0.t.sol:8-35 states the same round trip and the source text satisfies it.

cleared.check: BalanceDelta and BeforeSwapDelta packing and unpacking, and the arithmetic on packed deltas.
cleared.result: toBalanceDelta shifts amount0 left by 128 bits and masks amount1 to 128 bits, so sign extension bits of a negative amount1 cannot reach amount0 (src/types/BalanceDelta.sol:14-18). amount0 is read with sar 128 and amount1 with signextend 15 (BalanceDelta.sol:61-71). add and sub split both operands, add or subtract the halves as 256 bit numbers and pass each half through SafeCast.toInt128, which reverts when the result leaves the int128 range (BalanceDelta.sol:20-46, src/libraries/SafeCast.sol:40-43). A carry from the low half therefore cannot enter the high half. BeforeSwapDelta uses the same layout with the specified amount in the high half (src/types/BeforeSwapDelta.sol:9-37). A Python transcription returned the inputs for 200,000 random int128 pairs and for the extreme pairs. The hook delta that reaches these functions is a full word chosen by the hook, and both halves are valid int128 values by construction, so no bit pattern is out of range.

cleared.check: Fee fields: LP fee bounds and flag bits, the two 12 bit protocol fee halves, the combined swap fee and the unchecked subtraction of the protocol share.
cleared.result: MAX_LP_FEE is 1,000,000, which is below 2^20, so a valid fee never touches bit 22 (override flag 0x400000) or bit 23 (dynamic flag 0x800000) (src/libraries/LPFeeLibrary.sol:15-25). A pool is dynamic only when the fee field equals 0x800000 exactly (LPFeeLibrary.sol:30-32). isValidProtocolFee masks the low and the high 12 bits and compares them with 1001 and 1001 << 12 (src/libraries/ProtocolFeeLibrary.sol:25-32). I checked the function against the plain rule for one seventh of all 2^24 inputs. calculateSwapFee masks both inputs and returns p + l - floor(p * l / 1e6) (ProtocolFeeLibrary.sol:38-46). For every p from 0 to 1000 and a grid of l up to 1,000,000 the result stayed at or below 1,000,000 and was at least p and at least l, and it equalled p only when l was 0. The step fee is at least amountIn * swapFee / (1e6 - swapFee) rounded up, or the whole remainder on a partial step (src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:72-82, 104), so the protocol share floor((amountIn + feeAmount) * p / 1e6) cannot exceed it and the unchecked subtraction at src/libraries/Pool.sol:391-396 cannot wrap. The Slot0 setter masks the protocol fee to 24 bits before storing it (src/types/Slot0.sol:78-86).

cleared.check: Hook return data: which bits of the returned words the PoolManager uses, and whether dirty bits in a hook answer can change a value outside that hook's own pool.
cleared.result: parseSelector, parseFee and parseReturnDelta each load one full word at offsets 0x20, 0x60 and 0x40 of the returned bytes (src/libraries/ParseBytes.sol:9-28). The selector is compared as bytes4, so only the first four bytes of the first word count (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152). The fee word is used only for a dynamic fee pool and only through an AND with 0x400000, an AND with 0xBFFFFF and a comparison with 1,000,000 (Hooks.sol:263, src/libraries/LPFeeLibrary.sol:61-78, src/libraries/Pool.sol:303-305), so bits above bit 23 are dropped whatever the compiler does with the assembly assignment, and a returned dynamic flag makes the fee fail validation. The delta word is split into two int128 halves and applied with checked arithmetic (Hooks.sol:266-279, 295-313). The hook is credited exactly what the caller is debited (src/PoolManager.sol:181-183, 224-226). Every value a hook can influence stays inside the pool that names that hook. The length rules are at least 32 bytes for every hook, exactly 64 bytes when a delta is parsed and exactly 96 bytes for beforeSwap (Hooks.sol:152, 166, 259).

cleared.check: Hook flag bits and the validity rule: do the 14 flags overlap, does operator precedence give the intended test, and which special addresses pass the rule.
cleared.result: The 14 flags are the single bits 13 down to 0 and ALL_HOOK_MASK is 2^14 - 1 (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:27-47). In Solidity the bitwise AND binds tighter than the comparison, so hasPermission tests (address & flag) != 0 and the last line of isValidHookAddress tests (address & mask) > 0 (Hooks.sol:126, 337-339). I enumerated all 16,384 low bit patterns. With a static fee exactly 5,183 are accepted, which is 3^4 * 2^6 - 1: each of the four return delta bits needs its action bit, and the all zero pattern is refused. The zero address is accepted only with a static fee, and an address without flags only with the dynamic fee value (Hooks.sol:124-126). The fixed cases in test/libraries/Hooks.t.sol:940-990 agree, including the refusal of an address whose only set bit is bit 14. Low addresses that pass include 0x10, 0x64, 0x100 and 0x101. A precompile or a codeless account at such an address cannot answer with 32 bytes that start with the hook selector, so the hooked action of that pool reverts (Hooks.sol:152-154). That is the recorded hook trust finding F-004 and needs victims to choose a pool with that hook address. The identity precompile at 0x04 echoes its input and would pass the selector test, and its address carries bit 2 without bit 6, which the rule refuses (Hooks.sol:112).

cleared.check: Tick bitmap word and bit positions, the compress function, and the unchecked int24 products in the search for the next initialized tick.
cleared.result: position returns the signed tick shifted right by 8 as the word index and the low 8 bits as the bit index (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:35-41). flipTick rejects a tick that is not a multiple of the spacing, divides, and builds the mapping slot from the 256 bit sign extended word index and the mapping slot, which is the encoding Solidity uses for an int16 index (TickBitmap.sol:47-75). For 200,000 random ticks and spacings the assembly compress equalled floor division, and the word index stayed inside int16 (-3466 to 3465 at spacing 1). The lte mask keeps bitPos + 1 low bits and the other mask clears the bits below bitPos (TickBitmap.sol:97, 110). The literal 1 in 1 << bitPos is evaluated as uint256. The largest magnitude the unchecked products can reach is 256 * 32767 = 8,388,352 for word index -1 at the maximum spacing, which is inside int24 (limit 8,388,608), and the swap loop then clamps the result to MIN_TICK and MAX_TICK (src/libraries/Pool.sol:351-356). MAX_TICK_SPACING is int16 max and initialize enforces the range 1 to 32767 (src/libraries/TickMath.sol:26-28, src/PoolManager.sol:119-120).

cleared.check: Tick info packing, LiquidityMath.addDelta and the liquidity cap per tick: can a width error let one account overflow gross, net or in range liquidity.
cleared.result: updateTick stores liquidityGross masked to 128 bits in the low half and liquidityNet shifted into the high half, which matches the declaration order of TickInfo (src/libraries/Pool.sol:68-77, 544-557). liquidityNet is computed with checked int128 arithmetic before the store (Pool.sol:543). addDelta masks x to 128 bits, sign extends y from 128 bits and reverts when any bit above bit 127 is set in the sum, which covers both overflow and underflow (src/libraries/LiquidityMath.sol:10-19). A transcription agreed with exact integer arithmetic on 200,000 random cases with dirty upper bits in x. tickSpacingToMaxLiquidityPerTick reproduces the four values in test/Tick.t.sol:115-141. For every spacing from 1 to 32767 the cap times the number of usable ticks is below 2^128 and the cap is below 2^127, so the sum of all tick liquidity fits uint128 and liquidityNet fits int128.

cleared.check: ERC-6909 id to currency conversion in mint and burn, and whether an id with high bits set can reach a balance or allowance of another id.
cleared.result: mint and burn truncate the id to 160 bits with fromId and use the truncated currency for the delta and toId of it for the claim balance, so an id with high bits set acts on the canonical id (src/PoolManager.sol:322-336, src/types/Currency.sol:110-118). The allowance and operator check in _burnFrom uses the same canonical id and the caller as spender (src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22). transfer, transferFrom and approve use the raw 256 bit id (src/ERC6909.sol:25-56). A balance at an id with high bits can never be minted, so those ids always hold zero and every transfer of them reverts in the checked subtraction. mint casts the amount with toInt128 before the negation, so the unchecked block at PoolManager.sol:323-328 cannot wrap (src/libraries/SafeCast.sol:56-59). The interface id 0x0f632fb3 equals the XOR of the seven ERC-6909 selectors.

cleared.check: Transient slot constants, the hash used for delta slots and the nonzero delta counter.
cleared.result: With a keccak implementation written for this unit and checked against the known digest of the empty string, keccak256 of ReservesOf, Currency, NonzeroDeltaCount and Unlocked minus one equal the four constants (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:11-13, src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:9-10, src/libraries/Lock.sol:8). A delta slot is keccak256 of the 64 bytes (target, currency), both masked to 160 bits, in the same order in getDelta and applyDelta (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:10-41). A delta slot equal to a fixed slot would need a preimage of a hash minus one. sync stores the currency masked to 160 bits together with the reserves, and resetCurrency clears only the currency (CurrencyReserves.sol:21-32). applyDelta adds with checked int256 arithmetic. _accountDelta returns early for a zero delta, decrements the counter only when a slot returns to zero and increments only when it leaves zero, so the wrapping subtraction in decrement is never reached at zero (src/PoolManager.sol:368-378, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:28-34).

cleared.check: Position hash and pool id: byte layout of the assembly, dirty bits in the owner, and whether two different inputs can share a slot.
cleared.result: calculatePositionKey writes salt at offset 0x26, tickUpper at 0x06, tickLower at 0x03 and owner at 0 of free memory and hashes 58 bytes from offset 0x0c (src/libraries/Position.sol:54-66). I simulated the four overlapping writes on dirty memory for 2,000 random inputs with garbage above bit 160 of the owner. The result always equalled keccak256 of owner (20 bytes), tickLower (3), tickUpper (3) and salt (32), so the fields do not overlap and bits above the address fall outside the hashed range. The three words are zeroed afterwards. The owner is always msg.sender (src/PoolManager.sol:161). The pool id is keccak256 of the five words of the PoolKey in memory (src/types/PoolId.sol:11-15). The struct reaches memory through the ABI decoder of the external functions, which rejects dirty address, uint24 and int24 words, so one logical pool has one id.

cleared.check: Assembly memory use and cleanup: the ERC-20 transfer block, the hook call, the wrapped revert, the scratch space users and the storage readers.
cleared.result: The ERC-20 transfer writes 68 bytes at the free memory pointer without moving it, evaluates the call before the return data test, accepts empty return data or at least 32 bytes whose first word is 1, and zeroes the three words it used (src/types/Currency.sol:55-80). The output area is scratch word 0, and with empty return data the test does not read it. callHook allocates 32 bytes plus the return size rounded up to 32 after the call, which I checked for sizes 0 to 399, and copies the full return data (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:140-149). bubbleUpAndRevertWith lays out selector, address, selector word, the two offsets 0x80 and 0xa0 plus the padded size, the reason and a 4 byte context, and then reverts, so its use of memory past the pointer has no later reader (src/libraries/CustomRevert.sol:83-119). The delta slot hash and flipTick use only bytes 0 to 63 (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:11-15, src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:67-70). The revert helpers that take one argument write bytes 0 to 0x23, which is still scratch space (CustomRevert.sol:14-46). Extsload and Exttload return directly from assembly and write nothing but memory (src/Extsload.sol:10-63, src/Exttload.sol:10-39). No block writes below the free memory pointer outside the scratch space.
cleared.source: src/types/Currency.sol:40-88; src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-155; src/libraries/CustomRevert.sol:14-119; src/libraries/Position.sol:54-66; src/Extsload.sol:10-63; src/Exttload.sol:10-39

cleared.check: Every cast and every unchecked block in the non-test sources (30 occurrences of unchecked, 104 of assembly): can a wrap or a truncation give a caller a larger credit or a smaller debit.
cleared.result: take, mint and clear negate a value that toInt128 has limited to 0 through 2^127 - 1 (src/PoolManager.sol:292-296, 313-318, 323-328, src/libraries/SafeCast.sol:56-59). settle computes the payment with checked subtraction and casts it with toInt128 (PoolManager.sol:360-364). The unchecked protocol fee counter can only grow by amounts a swapper paid (src/ProtocolFees.sol:66-70). In Pool.swap the exact input remainder moves toward zero by at most its own size, the exact output remainder is reduced by at most itself, the protocol share is at most the step fee, the fee growth product stays below 2^255 because the whole swap amount must pass toInt128 at the end, and the final casts are function calls that revert inside the unchecked block (src/libraries/Pool.sol:371-407, 451-462). donate casts both amounts before negating (Pool.sol:469-479). The unchecked fee growth subtractions are modular by design and feed FullMath.mulDiv with a 128 bit liquidity and a divisor of 2^128, which cannot overflow (Pool.sol:497-510, 606-611, src/libraries/Position.sol:92-97). SafeCast compares the truncated value with the input for every narrowing cast (SafeCast.sol:16-59). The remaining unchecked blocks are in the math libraries that the two math units of cycle 1 and the two flow units of this cycle replayed. I found no cast or unchecked operation whose result an ordinary caller can push out of range without a revert.

cleared.check: Recount of every hex literal of six or more digits, the error selectors written as literals, and the TickMath and BitMath constants.
cleared.result: A script listed all such literals in the non-test sources. Each address mask has 40 digits of f, each 128 bit mask 32, each 24 bit mask 6, and the two selector masks keep the top four bytes. The literals 0xa9059cbb, 0x93dafdf1, 0xd4d8f3e6, 0xf5c787f1, 0x4323a555, 0x4f2461b8 and 0x00bfc921 equal the first four hash bytes of transfer(address,uint256), SafeCastOverflow(), TickMisaligned(int24,int24), PriceOverflow(), NotEnoughLiquidity(), InvalidPriceOrLiquidity() and InvalidPrice(). Each of the 20 TickMath multipliers read from the file is within 0.5 of 2^128 divided by sqrt(1.0001)^(2^i). With those constants getSqrtPriceAtTick is strictly increasing over all 1,774,545 ticks, returns MIN_SQRT_PRICE and MAX_SQRT_PRICE at the ends, and getTickAtSqrtPrice inverts it at every tick and one unit below. The two BitMath functions returned the exact bit index for every single bit value, every low and high mask and 200,000 random values. This repeats the cycle 1 result with a separate transcription.
cleared.source: src/libraries/TickMath.sol:20-36, 57-114, 121-237; src/libraries/BitMath.sol:12-48; src/types/Currency.sol:60; src/libraries/LiquidityMath.sol:15; src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:59; src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:66, 111, 140, 199

cleared.check: Do the 21 networks execute the bit level instructions of this unit as the code expects, and what do codeless and precompile targets return to a transfer shaped call.
cleared.result: I sent one 980 byte creation payload with eth_call and no to address to the RPC endpoint of each network in state/networks.json on 2026-11-22. It returns 28 words: SIGNEXTEND 15 and 2 on values with dirty upper bits, SAR 128, the BalanceDelta pack of (-5, -7), a Slot0 tick read, the delta slot hash, TLOAD before and after TSTORE, SDIV and SMOD of MIN_TICK by 60, a BYTE table lookup, SHL, SHR by 256, MULMOD by 2^256 - 1 and a 160 bit AND. It also makes four calls with the 68 byte calldata of transfer(address,uint256) and a 32 byte output area at memory 0. All 21 networks returned the 28 expected words. A codeless address and the ecrecover precompile at 0x01 return success with empty return data and leave memory word 0 unchanged. The identity precompile at 0x04 returns the 68 input bytes, whose first word is not 1, and sha256 at 0x02 returns a 32 byte hash. Under src/types/Currency.sol:64-74 a take in currency 0x01 or in a codeless currency therefore counts as paid and moves nothing, which only debits the caller (src/PoolManager.sol:294-295), and a take in currency 0x02 or 0x04 reverts. sync decodes a 32 byte result, so it reverts on empty data and reads a constant on 0x02 and 0x04, and the difference between sync and settle is then zero (Currency.sol:94, PoolManager.sol:358-360). No positive delta arises without a real balance increase on any of the 21 networks through these targets.
cleared.source: eth_call on the 21 rpc URLs in research/network-risk/state/networks.json; src/types/Currency.sol:55-80, 90-96; src/PoolManager.sol:279-297, 349-364

cleared.check: Storage layout assumed by StateLibrary, and the content of Owned.sol now that lib/solmate is checked out at commit 4b47a19.
cleared.result: Owned declares one storage variable, owner, an onlyOwner modifier that requires msg.sender == owner, a constructor and transferOwnership (lib/solmate/src/auth/Owned.sol:17-43). In the inheritance order of PoolManager the slots are owner 0, protocolFeesAccrued 1, protocolFeeController 2, isOperator 3, balanceOf 4, allowance 5 and _pools 6 (src/ProtocolFees.sol:15-24, src/ERC6909.sol:15-19, src/PoolManager.sol:80-93). NoDelegateCall holds only an immutable. POOLS_SLOT is 6 and the offsets 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6 match the fields of Pool.State (src/libraries/StateLibrary.sol:11-28, src/libraries/Pool.sol:83-91). remappings.txt maps solmate/ to lib/solmate/ and the repository holds no other Owned.sol.

cleared.check: Compiler bugs listed for solc 0.8.26: does the source text contain the patterns that the Solidity bug list names, in particular the Yul optimizer bug SOL-2026-7 of 22 October 2026.
cleared.result: bugs_by_version.json lists eight entries for 0.8.26. Seven need constructs the non-test sources do not contain: a recursive storage struct with a dynamic array (two entries), a custom error with named arguments inside require (the four require calls at src/libraries/FullMath.sol:30, 113 and src/libraries/BitMath.sol:13, 32 have no error argument), delete on a bytes element under the legacy pipeline, mutual recursion (two entries), and a storage array at the end of storage. SOL-2026-7 needs a variable that is used to compute memory or storage addresses, is reassigned in a loop or branch, and yields two addresses with different constant offsets that coincide at run time, followed by a load or an equal store. In the handwritten assembly the only reassigned address variables are memptr, startSlot and calldataptr in the loops of src/Extsload.sol:18-63 and src/Exttload.sol:18-39. Those functions never read back what they stored and never store a value twice, so neither affected optimizer step has anything to replace. Every other block derives its addresses from constants or from a pointer assigned once (src/types/Currency.sol:57, src/libraries/Position.sol:55, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:142, src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:67-73, src/libraries/Pool.sol:547). Storage and memory structs are reached through hashed mapping slots or pointers that are assigned once, and the swap loop changes no address variable by a constant (Pool.sol:344-437). The Solidity team states that the condition cannot be decided from Solidity source because it depends on the intermediate Yul code. I did not compile anything, so the compiler generated code remains unchecked and lead L-028 stays open.

cleared.check: Do the repository tests that state bit level expectations and revert conditions hold against the source text, for the files no earlier unit replayed.
cleared.result: I read the expectations and checked each against the source. test/types/Slot0.t.sol and test/types/BalanceDelta.t.sol hold on the transcriptions described above. test/CurrencyReserves.t.sol:32-41 expects the reserves to stay at 100 after resetCurrency, which matches src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:21-25. test/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.t.sol:22-41 expects wrapping, which matches the assembly. test/libraries/PoolId.t.sol expects keccak256 of the ABI encoding. test/libraries/SafeCast.t.sol states the six revert bounds of SafeCast.sol. test/libraries/Hooks.t.sol:191-990 uses 14 permission bits and the mask ~0 << 14 from test/utils/Deployers.sol:75-76 and the validity cases agree with my enumeration. test/PoolManagerInitialize.t.sol:55-85 expects the revert order tick spacing too large, too small, currency order, hook address, fee, which is the order of src/PoolManager.sol:119-128. test/PoolManager.clear.t.sol expects a revert unless the amount equals the positive delta and no change for zero on zero, which matches PoolManager.sol:310-319 and 369. The expectRevert cases of test/PoolManager.t.sol:96-1039, test/NoDelegateCall.t.sol, test/ERC6909Claims.t.sol, test/DynamicFees.t.sol:224-241 and test/CustomAccounting.t.sol:197-209 name the error the source raises at that point. I found no expectation that the source text cannot meet beyond the two already recorded in F-006. I read the tests and did not run them.

The non-test sources contain no receive or fallback function, no delegatecall, no SELFDESTRUCT, no CREATE, no use of block fields, tx.origin or gasleft, and the only payable functions are settle and settleFor (src/PoolManager.sol:300-307). leads.question: When this checkout is compiled with solc 0.8.26 and the foundry.toml settings, does the optimized Yul of PoolManager.swap, modifyLiquidity and the ABI coders contain a variable that is reassigned in a loop or branch and then used with two different constant offsets as a memory or storage address, as the Solidity team's reproducer test reassigned_offset_base.yul does?
leads.why: The source level screen of this unit covers only the handwritten assembly. The Solidity team says the condition for SOL-2026-7 depends on the intermediate Yul code. A positive answer would mean a stale load or a dropped store in code that moves pool funds on all 21 networks. It needs a compiler and can be done on this repository alone, with --ir-optimized output, without any other copy.

leadResults.answer: lib/solmate is checked out at commit 4b47a19 in this session. Owned.sol declares one storage variable, owner. onlyOwner is require(msg.sender == owner, "UNAUTHORIZED"). The constructor sets the owner and transferOwnership, guarded by onlyOwner, is the only other state changing function (lib/solmate/src/auth/Owned.sol:17-43). In the PoolManager the owner role reaches only setProtocolFeeController (src/ProtocolFees.sol:29-32).

transferOwnership writes the new owner in one step and emits OwnershipTransferred. There is no pending owner, no renounce function and no check that the new owner is nonzero (lib/solmate/src/auth/Owned.sol:39-43).

Besides setProtocolFeeController (src/ProtocolFees.sol:29-32) the owner can only call transferOwnership (lib/solmate/src/auth/Owned.sol:39-43). No other function in src/ uses onlyOwner or reads owner.

lib/solmate is no longer empty. remappings.txt maps solmate/ to lib/solmate/, the submodule is at 4b47a19038b798b4a33d9749d25e570443520647, and it is the only Owned.sol in the repository. ProtocolFees uses only the constructor and the onlyOwner modifier of Owned (src/ProtocolFees.sol:26-29). The ERC-20 transfer in src/types/Currency.sol:55-80 is the repository's own assembly and does not use solmate.

First half answered: Owned declares exactly one storage variable, so _pools is at slot 6 as StateLibrary.POOLS_SLOT assumes (lib/solmate/src/auth/Owned.sol:17, src/ProtocolFees.sol:21-24, src/ERC6909.sol:15-19, src/PoolManager.sol:93, src/libraries/StateLibrary.sol:11). Second half open: I did not examine the Unichain predeploy, because the owner has ruled out comparing this code with other copies.

I fetched the Solidity team's post and the bug list. The handwritten assembly in src/ does not contain the reproducer pattern: the only address variables that are reassigned sit in the loops of Extsload and Exttload, which never load what they stored, and every other block uses constant addresses or a pointer assigned once. The other seven entries listed for 0.8.26 need constructs that src/ does not contain. The condition on the intermediate Yul code of the compiler generated parts cannot be decided from the text, and I had no compiler, so the bytecode comparison the lead asks for is still open.

For the bit level files and the revert cases I found no expectation that the source text fails. Covered by reading and, where numeric, by transcription: test/types/Slot0.t.sol, test/types/BalanceDelta.t.sol, test/CurrencyReserves.t.sol, test/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.t.sol, test/libraries/PoolId.t.sol, the revert bounds of test/libraries/SafeCast.t.sol, the validity and permission cases of test/libraries/Hooks.t.sol:191-990, the revert order of test/PoolManagerInitialize.t.sol:55-85 and its fixed cases, test/PoolManager.clear.t.sol, test/NoDelegateCall.t.sol, the expectRevert cases of test/ERC6909Claims.t.sol and of test/PoolManager.t.sol:96-1039. Not covered by this unit: the hook call sequences in test/libraries/Hooks.t.sol:46-190 and 992-1046 beyond their revert selectors, test/libraries/FullMath.t.sol and Position.t.sol, test/ModifyLiquidity.t.sol, the liquidity section of test/CustomAccounting.t.sol and the value assertions of test/ERC6909Claims.t.sol. I read the tests and did not run them.
